---
title: Graph and geometry
---

Atom i of a graph is atom i of its geometry. Every routine crosses between the two: it
seeds a structure from the graph, and checks each structure it gets back against the graph.

Geometries are autogeom's `Geometry`, which carries `charge` and `spin` too.

::: {.callout-note}
Planned: Phase 2 (`embed`) and Phase 3 (`stereo_matches`).
:::

## Seeding a structure

```python
geo = pm.embed(smg)               # RDKit ETKDG, with the graph's stereo and atom order
```

## Checking a structure

A conformer search or an optimization can invert a centre or flip a bond. A structure is
kept only if it is still the workflow's stereoisomer:

```python
pm.stereo_matches(smg, geo)       # LS parities read from the coordinates
```

## Perceiving a graph

For a structure from outside a workflow (an INCITE geometry, an IRC end point), the atom
order is kept. The LS sites are the low-T ones `from_smiles` gives, and every parity is
read from the coordinates, so the graph describes this structure atom for atom:

```python
>>> import autogeom as ag
>>> import protomol as pm
>>> geo = ag.from_smiles(r"C[C@@H](O)/C=C/C")  # stands in for an outside structure
>>> gra = pm.from_geometry(geo)
>>> gra.symbols[:5], (gra.charge, gra.spin), pm.is_determined(gra)
(('C', 'C', 'O', 'C', 'C'), (0, 0), True)
>>> pm.canonical_json(gra) == pm.canonical_json(pm.examples.species())
True
>>> pm.display(gra, atom_indices=True)  # doctest: +SKIP

```

Renumbering the geometry renumbers the graph the same way. A mirror-image structure gives
the enantiomer:

```python
>>> mirror = pm.from_geometry(ag.reflect(geo, [0.0, 0.0, 1.0]))
>>> pm.canonical_json(mirror) == pm.canonical_json(pm.from_smiles(r"C[C@H](O)/C=C/C"))
True

```
